title: MatterSim-MT: Multi-Task Materials Foundation Model Up to 5,000 K & 1,000 GPa
aiSystem: MatterSim-MT (Microsoft Research Multi-Task Atomistic Foundation Model)
whyItMatters: Pretrained on >35M first-principles structures across 89 elements up to 5,000 K and 1,000 GPa, unifying atomistic dynamics with phonons, dielectric tensors, ferroelectric hysteresis, and battery cathode redox in one model.
summary: Microsoft Research AI for Science introduced MatterSim-MT (May 2026, building on MatterSim 2024), a multi-task atomistic foundation model pretrained on over 35 million actively sampled first-principles structures spanning 89 elements, temperatures up to 5,000 K, and pressures up to 1,000 GPa. Moving beyond scalar potential-energy surfaces alone, MatterSim-MT jointly predicts energies, forces, Bader charges, magnetic moments, Born effective charges, and dielectric matrices—reproducing pressure-dependent LO–TO phonon splitting in SiC (~1 THz max phonon error), ferroelectric hysteresis in BaTiO₃, and cationic-to-anionic redox transitions in Li-rich battery cathodes.
technicalHighlights: Trained via active-learning MD + DFT across >35M structures spanning 89 elements, 0–5,000 K, and 0–1,000 GPa—far beyond ambient-condition datasets.
Multi-task heads jointly predict Born effective charges, dielectric matrices, Bader charges, and magnetic moments alongside interatomic forces.
Reproduced experimental LO–TO phonon splitting in SiC, electric hysteresis in ferroelectric BaTiO₃, and anionic redox during Li-rich cathode delithiation.
caveats: Released as an arXiv preprint undergoing active community evaluation; extreme-condition predictions outside DFT training regimes still benefit from uncertainty-guided active-learning fine-tuning.
contributors: MatterSim Team (Microsoft Research AI for Science)

scoreRationale.foundational: Unifies extreme-temperature/pressure interatomic potentials with electronic, dielectric, and magnetic property tensors in one foundation model.
scoreRationale.ripple: Enables end-to-end in-silico characterization of ferroelectrics, extreme-pressure phases, and next-gen battery cathodes.
scoreRationale.verification: Extensive first-principles and experimental benchmarks in arXiv:2605.07927, though still preprint pending journal peer review.
scoreRationale.velocity: Replaces disparate DFT/DFPT calculations for phonons, Born charges, and phase diagrams with unified multi-task inference.
